extra.message: Reflected XSS: The 'name' value originates from the unsanitized GET parameter request.args.get('name') in app/blueprints/sandboxes/views.py:13 and is rendered with the Jinja2 '| safe' filter, which disables HTML auto-escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript via the ?name= parameter (e.g., ?name=<script>alert(1)</script>).

extra.message: Reflected/Stored XSS: The 'name' value originates from an attacker-controllable cookie request.cookies.get('name') or form field request.form.get('name') in app/blueprints/sandboxes/views.py:27-28 and is rendered with the Jinja2 '| safe' filter, disabling auto-escaping. The value is also written back into the 'name' cookie (views.py:38), allowing persistent script injection.

The message content is supplied by user input via the unauthenticated API endpoint POST /api/v1/messages (app/blueprints/api/views.py:43-54, no auth decorator) and via the feedback form (app/blueprints/account_area/views.py:66-77). An attacker can store JavaScript that executes in the admin's browser when they view messages.

The from_user value is fully attacker-controlled via the unauthenticated API endpoint POST /api/v1/messages where data.get('from_user') is stored unsanitized (app/blueprints/api/views.py:50-52). extra.message: Open Redirect: The 'next' query parameter is read from request.args.get('next') and passed directly to redirect() without validating that it points to a local/allowed URL. An attacker can craft a link like /toggle_xss_protection/?next=https://evil.com to redirect victims to an arbitrary external site (phishing).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: Missing Authentication / Authorization: The MessagesView.post() endpoint (POST /api/v1/messages) has no @admin_required or @login_required decorator, unlike the other Message endpoints. Any unauthenticated attacker can inject arbitrary messages with attacker-controlled 'message' and 'from_user' fields, which are then rendered unescaped in the admin panel (stored XSS vector).

Broken Access Control / type-confusion in is_owning_user: it compares user.id (an integer from the DB) with 'id' which is the URL path segment passed as a string from UsersView.get/put (app/blueprints/api/views.py:77,98). The strict '==' between int and str will not behave as a robust ownership check, and combined with the weak authorization model, can lead to inconsistent access decisions on per-user resources (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Sensitive Data Exposure: User.serialize includes the plaintext 'password' field in its output. This serialized data is returned by the API endpoints UsersView.index (GET /api/v1/users) and could be exposed to clients, leaking all users' passwords.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Cleartext Storage of Password: The User.password column stores passwords as plaintext (no hashing). Passwords are also compared in cleartext at app/blueprints/login/views.py:17 (user.password == password) and app/blueprints/account_area/views.py:26. A database compromise immediately exposes all credentials.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: Hardcoded Credentials: The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as a static string 'Keep it secret, keep it safe'. Since this key signs session cookies, anyone who knows it (it is committed to source) can forge session cookies and impersonate users, including bypassing authentication.

Security Misconfiguration: Flask DEBUG mode is enabled (app.config['DEBUG'] = True). In debug mode Flask exposes the interactive Werkzeug debugger which allows arbitrary Python code execution via the traceback console, and leaks stack traces / source code on errors. This must never be enabled in production.

Security Misconfiguration: The after_request handler explicitly sets the 'X-XSS-Protection' response header to 0 (disabled) by default unless a session flag is set. Disabling the browser's XSS auditor removes a defense-in-depth control and increases exploitability of the reflected/stored XSS issues in this app.

Security Misconfiguration: The application never sets SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY, SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, or SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE. Combined with the XSS issues, session cookies may be accessible to injected JavaScript and transmitted over insecure channels. The 'name' cookie set in sandboxes/views.py:38 is likewise set without HttpOnly/Secure flags.

Improper Error Handling / DoS: MessagesView.get() calls .first().serialize before checking for None. If no message matches the supplied id, .first() returns None and accessing .serialize raises AttributeError, causing an unhandled 500 error (the subsequent 'if not message' check is unreachable for this case). An attacker can trigger errors with arbitrary ids.
